title: Discount curve and forward discounting check

items.prompt: What does a deterministic curve node D(0,3) = 0.94 mean?

options.label: At time zero, 0.94 currency units buy one currency unit paid at model-year 3
At model-year 3, 0.94 currency units are paid at time zero
The annual rate is 94% under every compounding convention

items.explanation: A discount factor is a dated price ratio. It is not itself an annualized rate quotation.

items.prompt: Can a valid supplied curve contain D(0,1) = 1.01 in this lesson?

options.label: Yes; a positive factor above one corresponds to a negative continuously compounded zero rate
No; every discount factor is mathematically restricted below one
Only if issuer default is certain

items.explanation: The domain requires positive factors, not factors below one. Negative rates can produce factors above one.

items.prompt: Given D(0,1) = 0.98 and D(0,3) = 0.94, calculate the forward discount factor Z(1,3).
Given D(0,2) = 0.95 and D(0,5) = 0.88, calculate the forward discount factor Z(2,5).
items.explanation: Z(2,5) = 0.88 / 0.95. The result is time-2 currency per one unit paid at time 5.
